sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Walworth County?
sections.html:
Your town, village or city treasurer collects the first payment, and the Walworth County Treasurer collects the second installment and every delinquent payment. The county treasurer is at the Government Center, 100 W Walworth Street, Room 103, Elkhorn, WI 53121. The phone number is 262-741-4251, and the office is open 8 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday.

Each municipality mails bills by mid-December. According to the county treasurer FAQ, you should call your local treasurer if no bill arrives by December 20. A missing bill does not excuse a late payment or the interest that follows.

sections.h2: When are Walworth County property taxes due and where do I pay?
sections.html:
Taxes are due January 31 to the local municipality, or in two installments with the second due July 31 to the county. If the total is under $100, the whole amount is due January 31.

SituationDeadlinePay to
Full paymentJanuary 31Local municipality
First installmentJanuary 31Local municipality
Second installmentJuly 31Walworth County Treasurer
Tax bill under $100January 31, all at onceLocal municipality
Anything paid after February 1As soon as possibleWalworth County Treasurer

The county's Pay Taxes page and Wis. Stat. 74.11 agree on these dates. Miss the first installment and the whole unpaid balance becomes delinquent as of February 1. The statute allows five working days after January 31 for a payment to be received.

sections.h2: How can I pay the Walworth County Treasurer?
sections.html:
You can pay in person, by mail, in the drop box or online. The drop box sits at the west end of the median in the parking lot on the north side of the building, close to the Elkhorn Police Station. Online payments run through the county's Ascent Land Records site around the clock.

The county lists these convenience fees:

  • Credit card: 2.29 percent per transaction, with a $2.00 minimum
  • Debit card: 1.5 percent per transaction, with a $2.00 minimum
  • E-check: $1.00 per transaction

In December and January the county treasurer cannot process real estate payments, so all payments in that window go through the municipality where the property sits. For mailed payments, include the stub from the bill or write the parcel number on the check. If you want a receipt for a mailed payment, enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope, and know that the receipt is not valid until the payment clears the banks. A copy of a bill costs $1, with a self-addressed stamped envelope, tax year and tax key number, mailed to P.O. Box 1001, Elkhorn, WI 53121.

sections.h2: What happens when Walworth County taxes are not paid?
sections.html:
Delinquent taxes carry 1 percent interest plus a 0.5 percent penalty each month, starting February 1, and a part of a month counts as a whole month. That adds up to 1.5 percent per month on the unpaid tax, and the county treasurer takes all of these payments.

The county warns that a property delinquent for two or more years is subject to foreclosure. Walworth County uses the in rem tax foreclosure procedure, which the county treasurer oversees. Under Wis. Stat. 75.521, the treasurer can file a list of liens with the circuit court two years after the tax certificate date. Anyone with an interest in a listed parcel may redeem by paying the sums in the list with interest and the county's costs, or may file a verified answer within 30 days after the last redemption date in the published notice. If no one redeems or answers, the court enters judgment vesting the property in the county.

An owner who plans to sell in this position should ask the treasurer for a payoff figure early, since costs grow as the case moves forward.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Walworth County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with your local assessor, because the county treasurer sends all assessment questions to the municipality. If the assessor does not resolve it, the next step is your municipal board of review.

Under Wis. Stat. 70.47, the board meets once a year during a 45-day window that starts on the fourth Monday of April. The board's rules include:

  • Give written or oral notice of your intent to object at least 48 hours before the first meeting
  • File a written objection within the first two hours of the first meeting
  • Bring evidence, because the assessor's value is presumed correct until you rebut it

You cannot skip the board. Under Wis. Stat. 74.37, a claim for an excessive assessment must be served on the municipal clerk by January 31 of the year the tax is payable. You must have followed the board of review process and paid the tax on time. The municipality has 90 days to answer, and if it denies the claim you have 90 days from the notice to sue in circuit court.

sections.h2: Which credits can Walworth County homeowners claim?
sections.html:
Two state credits show up on Walworth County bills. The lottery and gaming credit applies to owners whose primary residence was the home on January 1 of the year the tax is levied. The First Dollar Credit has applied to state taxable parcels with a real property improvement since the 2008 tax bill.

The county directs people to the Wisconsin Department of Revenue for the details of both. If your bill does not show a credit you think you qualify for, ask the county treasurer or your local treasurer how to apply.

sections.h2: What should sellers know about Walworth County?
sections.html:
Walworth County covers 577 square miles along the Illinois border, with Elkhorn as the county seat. The 2020 census counted 106,478 residents and 53,146 housing units, and 20.3 percent of the units were vacant. Among occupied homes, 31.1 percent were rented, which is a higher renter share than in the suburban counties to the north.

Tourism drives much of the local economy. Lake Geneva, Alpine Valley Resort and Alpine Valley Music Theatre draw visitors, and the county ranked sixth in the state for tourism impact, close to $1 billion in 2023. The University of Wisconsin-Whitewater is also here. The cities are Burlington, Delavan, Elkhorn, Lake Geneva and Whitewater, and the villages include Bloomfield, Darien, East Troy, Fontana-on-Geneva Lake, Genoa City, Mukwonago, Sharon, Walworth and Williams Bay.

Several of these places cross county lines. Burlington sits mostly in Racine County, Whitewater partly in Jefferson County, Genoa City partly in Kenosha County and Mukwonago mostly in Waukesha County. Check the county printed on your tax bill before you decide which treasurer to call.

Before a cash sale closes, ask the closing agent to request a current tax statement from the treasurer so that any balance for the year is settled at the table.

faqs.q: When are Walworth County property taxes due?
faqs.a: January 31 is the due date for the full tax or the first installment, and July 31 is the due date for the second installment. A bill under $100 must be paid in full by January 31. Pay the first payment to your local municipality and the second to the Walworth County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Where is the Walworth County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: It is at the Walworth County Government Center, 100 W Walworth Street, Room 103, Elkhorn, WI 53121, and the phone is 262-741-4251. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1001, Elkhorn, WI 53121. Hours are 8 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: How much interest does Walworth County charge on late taxes?
faqs.a: The county charges 1 percent interest and a 0.5 percent penalty each month, which totals 1.5 percent per month. The clock starts February 1, and any part of a month counts as a full month.

faqs.q: Can Walworth County foreclose on unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Property that is delinquent for two or more years is subject to foreclosure, and the county treasurer runs the in rem procedure. Interested parties can redeem by paying what is owed plus costs before the redemption deadline in the published notice.

faqs.q: Who handles questions about my Walworth County assessment?
faqs.a: Your local assessor does, and you can then go to your municipal board of review. The county treasurer does not set or change assessed values.
